actor: Accreditation scheme manager, CREST penetration testing standards team
job: Turning the July 28 Domain 7 and Annex B text into assessable requirements and processing the first applications through the scheme.
outcome: A named company published in CREST's accreditation listing as holding the AI-enabled penetration testing annex.
motivation: CREST said it expected a first accredited organisation within about a month, and an unheld standard accredits nobody.

task.who: CREST standards and accreditation operations staff
task.what: Publish assessor guidance for the AI annex
task.where: CREST company and penetration testing accreditation standards
task.why: Applications opened the day the standard published
task.how: Domain 7 and Annex B requirement mapping

actor: Lead assessor for AI-enabled penetration testing, CREST assessment panel
job: Assessing applicant firms against Domain 7 and Annex B by sampling their engagement records rather than their tooling claims.
outcome: An assessment report that clears a platform vendor for listing, or names the evidence gaps blocking it.
motivation: Independent assessment is the whole value of the artefact; a waved-through applicant would make the listing worth nothing.

task.who: CREST-appointed assessors working the applicant queue
task.what: Sample engagement files for human oversight evidence
task.where: Applicant scoping records, test reports and sign-off logs
task.why: The annex requires judgement, not tool output
task.how: Documentary review plus assessor interviews on site

actor: Compliance and accreditation programme lead, Horizon3.ai
job: Assembling the company application for CREST's AI additions and carrying it through assessment on Horizon3's own legal entity.
outcome: Horizon3 listed by CREST under Domain 7 and Annex B, not a partner or delivery affiliate.
motivation: Its payment-card offering already puts certified humans on the invoice; accreditation makes that signature independently assessed instead of self-asserted.

task.who: Horizon3 compliance function with legal and services leads
task.what: Submit the company application to CREST
task.where: CREST's application process for the company standard
task.why: Assessment takes quarters and the window is short
task.how: Evidence pack mapped clause by clause

actor: Responsible AI governance owner, autonomous penetration-testing platform vendor
job: Writing the organisational AI governance, oversight and transparency policy set that Domain 7 asks a provider to hold and evidence.
outcome: An approved AI use policy, model inventory and oversight register an assessor can test against Domain 7.
motivation: Domain 7 sits in the company general requirements, so no engagement-level work counts until the organisational governance exists.

task.who: Security governance and risk function inside the vendor
task.what: Draft the AI oversight and transparency policy
task.where: Company management system and internal policy register
task.why: Domain 7 gates the whole company application

actor: Offensive services delivery manager, Horizon3.ai certified testing practice
job: Standardising how the human testers scope, review and sign engagements so an assessor sampling any file finds the same record.
outcome: A consistent engagement file per client showing named tester accountability across scoping, review and the delivered report.
motivation: Annex B is about the conduct of the engagement, and an assessor samples files rather than reading a datasheet.

task.who: Certified testers and report QA reviewers at Horizon3
task.what: Rework engagement records for assessor sampling
task.where: Delivery workflow behind the customer test report
task.why: Assessors sample files, not capability claims
task.how: Standard scoping, review and sign-off templates

actor: Platform product manager for engagement audit trail, AI-driven penetration-testing vendor
job: Shipping the per-finding record that shows which output the platform produced and which qualified human reviewed and accepted it.
outcome: Exportable evidence attributing every reported finding to a named reviewer, ready for an assessor to sample.
motivation: The annex is written so AI enhances professional judgement, and only the product can prove where the judgement happened.

task.who: Platform engineering team owning reporting and audit logs
task.what: Add reviewer attribution to every reported finding
task.where: Reporting pipeline and the customer-facing findings export
task.why: Human judgement must be evidenced, not asserted
task.how: Immutable review log exported with the report

actor: Compliance programme lead, UK-headquartered AI-driven penetration-testing platform vendor
job: Moving early on the AI annex while CREST's home-market framework buyers are already writing accreditation into their renewal requirements.
outcome: A CREST-listed platform vendor outside the United States holding the AI annex before the larger US-anchored competitors.
motivation: CREST's pull is heaviest in the United Kingdom, the Gulf and Singapore, where the accreditation already clears procurement.

task.who: Compliance and bid team at the UK vendor
task.what: Apply under the new AI annex early
task.where: CREST company and penetration testing applications
task.why: Home-market tenders already ask for CREST accreditation
task.how: Existing CREST membership extended to the annex

actor: Third-party assurance lead, regulated-enterprise security procurement
job: Rewriting penetration-testing tender requirements so an AI-run engagement must come from a firm accredited under the new annex.
outcome: Purchase orders and tenders that name the AI annex, giving platform vendors a revenue reason to apply.
motivation: Its auditors accept an accountable signature rather than a capability claim, and the annex is the first assessed artefact.

task.who: Security assurance and procurement function at the buyer
task.what: Add the AI annex to tender requirements
task.where: Penetration testing tender and supplier assurance questionnaires
task.why: Auditors accept an assessed accreditation, not marketing
task.how: Supplier accreditation clause in the standard contract

actor: Corporate development lead, venture-funded autonomous penetration-testing platform company
job: Spending Series E proceeds to buy or build the accredited testing entity, then holding the accreditation on the platform company.
outcome: The accreditation recorded against the platform company itself rather than a reseller, partner or delivery affiliate.
motivation: A bundled meter cannot ship an accountable signature, and a freshly repriced balance sheet can pay for one.

task.who: Corporate development with the general counsel's office
task.what: Model buy-versus-build for the accredited entity
task.where: Post-round capital allocation and diligence review
task.why: Accreditation must sit on the platform company
